assumptions: Exactly a natural-number inverse tower of finite free abelian groups with arbitrary linear transitions. No stage-to-colimit injection, transition injection or surjection is assumed.
quantifiers: Every such tower and every target abelian group A; equality of every pair of actual records; every homomorphism between target groups.
domains: FreeTower over Z encodes the prescribed finite free groups in ModuleCat. Record A is the actual Module.DirectLimit of Hom(P_n,A), and Invariant is Record Z. Its record_eq_iff is exactly equality after some common later stage. Universe-polymorphic ModuleCat supplies the fixed small-group universe, with natural transformations in the next universe.
conclusions: The actual direct limit provides well-defined addition; the exact representative equality is proved. Postcomposition gives a functor. The natural linear equivalence Invariant tensor A -> Record A has the stated pure-tensor formula and inverse. Invariant is countable and torsion-free, by eventual equality and torsion-freeness at the later finite free stage.
representation: The construction uses the actual finite free dual/tensor equivalence and mathlib direct-limit/tensor isomorphism. It never models a noninjective direct system as a union. Z-linear maps are exactly the group homomorphisms required by the task.

assumptions: Only S1 tower assumptions; arbitrary finite diagrams, including the empty diagram; arbitrary pairs of towers.
quantifiers: Every actual finite category and diagram, all natural transformations with homomorphism components, identities, composable pairs and all natural isomorphisms.
domains: The actual comparison sends a record to its projected compatible family. Finite object and arrow types provide a common later stage for all representatives and all equations. The categorical cone theorem covers the conventional finite-limit notion.
conclusions: Every record functor preserves every finite limit. All natural transformations are in bijection with Hom_Z(M_P,M_Pprime), identity corresponds to identity and categorical composition to reversed-order LinearMap.comp as required. Natural isomorphism is equivalent to isomorphism of the actual invariants.
representation: Naturality is checked over every small module, not a selected test collection. The tensor proof uses linearity to extend from pure tensors. The larger-universe equivalence only lifts the transformation type, preserving its domain of naturality.

assumptions: Exactly the original finite free countable tower; representation by an ordinary small abelian group, not a pro-object.
quantifiers: Both directions of every classification equivalence; every representing object; every small category whose objects and arrows are countable, and every diagram in it.
domains: M is the actual invariant colimit determined by the tower. The product comparison is the canonical coordinate-projection map, using ULift Z solely to match arbitrary universe levels. PreservesCountableLimits quantifies over both countable objects and countable hom-types; with countable objects this is the stated countable-arrow condition.
conclusions: Representation, preservation of all countable limits, surjectivity of the canonical countable integer product comparison, finite generation of M and finite freeness of M are equivalent. The representing objects are precisely the isomorphism class of M dual. Finite M gives preservation of every small limit. An additional finite-stage matrix/transition criterion is proved equivalent and is used for the rank-one classification.
representation: The noncircular necessity is proved by enumerating the actual countable M and using finite tensor support to obtain a finite generating set. No universal representability assumption is smuggled into the finite-stage criterion; it states actual transition equations. The complete natural transformation classification remains S2.

assumptions: The rank-one tower has actual stage Z and transition multiplication by an arbitrary integer a_n, including zero and negative values.
quantifiers: All integer sequences. Both directions of representation iff cofinal zeros or eventual units; all representing objects in each affirmative branch.
domains: CofinalZeros means every tail contains a zero. EventualUnits means every coefficient in some tail is a unit, and classification_with_signs spells this out as +1 or -1. These are the exact two task branches, not a nonzero-only restriction.
conclusions: Rank one alone does not imply representation: the actual doubling tower is a counterexample. The complete criterion is cofinally many zeros or eventual signs. Cofinal zeros give the actual zero record functor, represented by the zero group. An eventual-unit tail gives an actual invariant isomorphism with Z and a natural Hom(Z,-) representation. The full classes of representing objects are respectively zero and Z up to isomorphism. A nonzero tail with cofinal nonunits is not representable, hence its invariant is not finitely generated by S3.
representation: A valid alternative proof uses S3 finite-stage transition equations: every Z-linear idempotent on Z is zero or identity. The zero branch forces a later zero in every tail; the identity branch forces every later coefficient to be a unit. No division by a possibly zero coefficient or omitted finite prefix is used.

assumptions: The actual stable images I_n after a given N and the actual restricted-step isomorphisms, exactly as in S5. No purity, direct-summand or extension hypothesis is added.
quantifiers: Every admissible tower, cutoff N and family of actual submodules; all target groups and actual records. Existence of some later m with a retraction is distinguished from the false assertion at every n.
domains: The generic commutative-ring construction specializes to Z. hmap expresses that the restriction is defined and hb its bijectivity. ImageRealized is a weaker consequence, proved from the full eventual actual-image condition; it is not a representation or splitting assumption.
conclusions: The restricted transition isomorphisms define compatible actual threads from I_N. Evaluating an actual record along those threads gives a natural linear equivalence Record A = Hom(I_N,A); injectivity uses eventual actual images and surjectivity constructs a representative at a stage realizing I_N. At that stage J inverse composed with the actual transition is a retraction onto I_m. The explicit tower a_0=2, a_n=1 otherwise satisfies every premise while I_0=2Z has neither a retraction nor any direct complement in Z.
representation: The example uses actual ranges of the integer transition maps. Its eventual-image and restricted-step claims are proved, then the impossibility of retracting 2Z is derived from integer linearity. A complement would induce the forbidden projection. The general representation does not appeal circularly to S3 necessity or assume a current-stage splitting.

assumptions: Exactly the specified integer doubling tower, homomorphism-valued natural transformations, and the actual canonical integer-coordinate product comparison.
quantifiers: All natural endomorphisms, both directions of invertibility, every signed power with arbitrary integer exponent, and every possible preimage of the concrete reciprocal sequence.
domains: D is the actual subgroup of Q consisting of z/2^n. The genuine invariant equivalence is conjugated with the complete S2 natural-transformation equivalence. naturalEndEquiv is a bijection from all actual natural endomorphisms onto D; addition, identity and composition are separately proved to be rational addition, one and multiplication.
conclusions: The entire End ring is Z[1/2]. Actual natural automorphisms have exactly coefficients +/-2^k, k in Z; every such coefficient is constructed as an actual natural isomorphism. The target sequence is j |-> [j,id_Z], whose invariant value is 1/2^j. For a supposed source record at stage n, coordinate n+1 would imply 2*z=1 for an integer z, contradiction. Every finite limit is still preserved by S2.
representation: Integer linearity, rather than assumed Q-linearity, proves each dyadic endomorphism is multiplication by its value at one. Signed-unit necessity clears denominators and applies the prime-power divisor theorem. The missing product element proof works with actual common-stage records, so it does not confuse separate coordinate representatives with a uniform stage.
